numerical_failure.observed_behavior: On a 32-bit (i686) Debian machine with scipy 1.5.2, nnls on the issue reproducer returns badly diverging coefficients of magnitude around 1e15 to 1e16 (e.g. 3.83029964e+15, 1.15048400e+16, 1.14353389e+16, 1.33912811e+16, 5.49535003e+15) where the old implementation gives sensible values of order 1; on 64-bit systems the result is fine.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: coef should be sensible, matching the scipy 1.4.1 result on the same 32-bit machine: [0., 0., 1.05617285, 0., 0., 0., 0., 0.23123048, 0., 0., 0., 0.26128651]; the 64-bit result from both versions is described as similar to this.
trigger_conditions: X is 5x12 with first two rows set to zero (X[:2, :] = 0), generated with np.random.RandomState(42) randn
independent-column test in the NNLS solver (__nnls.c) using unorm + fabs(pivot)*0.01 - unorm > 0 suffers cancellation on 32-bit

input_output_examples.input: rng = np.random.RandomState(42); n_samples, n_features = 5, 12; X = rng.randn(n_samples, n_features); X[:2, :] = 0; y = rng.randn(n_samples); coef = nnls(X, y)[0]

oracle_clues: Issue reports coefficients compared against scipy 1.4.1 output on the same 32-bit machine
Fix PR replaces the independence test with a spacing-based test (spacing = nextafter(unorm, 2*unorm) - unorm; test fabs(pivot) > 100.0*spacing)
PR states the change is a no-op for 64-bit systems

numerical_characteristics.dtype: double (float64) arithmetic in the NNLS C implementation; the failure appears on 32-bit (i686) builds but not 64-bit
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: coefficients diverge to about 1e15-1e16 on the 32-bit machine, versus sensible values (around 0.2 to 1.06) on the reference and 64-bit runs
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: test uses assert_allclose with default tolerances against the expected coefficients [0, 0, 1.05617285, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0.23123048, 0, 0, 0, 0.26128651]; the separating tolerance value is not stated
category_specific_evidence: Issue #22791: nnls on a debian 32-bit (i686) machine gives badly diverging coef values around 1e15-1e16 with scipy 1.5.2, while scipy 1.4.1 gives sensible coef values; on a 64-bit machine both versions agree.
Reproducer uses numpy RandomState(42), X of shape 5x12 with the first two rows zeroed, and y of length 5 from randn.
PR #22802 title says it fixes instability with NNLS on 32-bit systems by changing the independent column test to a numerically more stable one.
Commit messages mention replacing an accumulator with BLAS ddot and using spacing (machine epsilon) for linear independence in NNLS.
Regression test test_gh_22791_32bit compares against the known-good coefficients using assert_allclose.
PR discussion says the change is a no-op for 64-bit systems and seems to fix the 32-bit issue.
reproduction_risks: The divergence only shows on 32-bit hardware or builds; a 64-bit run will not reproduce the failure and matches the fixed behavior.
The reproducer depends on the RandomState(42) draw order, so a different numpy version or RNG change could alter X and y.
The exact tolerance at which correct and incorrect answers separate is not stated in the passages.
The stdio.h include in the diff is an unrelated debugging artifact and is not part of the numerical cause.
